findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add child acceptance criteria that, whenever a new bridge diagnostic subverb is introduced, require it to have one coherent responsibility and a stable named result contract (with a schema/contract test), matching parent AC3.
evidence: Parent AC3: 'Any new bridge diagnostic subverb has one coherent responsibility and a stable named result contract.'

Child AC6: 'A new bridge diagnostic subcommand is introduced only if the observable-to-owner matrix proves a named current observable has no home in preview/fsck/status, and the ticket comment records that forcing case.'
Child AC6 delivers a precursor/gating outcome (when + record), not the same observable outcome (subverb responsibility coherence + stable named result contract).
No other sibling exists in the roster to deliver the remainder.
container pairing: parent + bec7-d2ff-79d0-40ff
findings.finding: Parent AC3 requires that ANY new bridge diagnostic subverb 'has one coherent responsibility and a stable named result contract', but the sole child's AC6 only governs the GATING condition (a new subcommand is introduced only when the matrix proves a named observable has no home) plus recording the forcing case. The child never requires the resulting subverb to have one coherent responsibility or a stable named result contract, so the parent's quality observable is only partially covered.
scenarios: The observable-to-owner matrix genuinely forces a new bridge diagnostic subverb; the child introduces and records it but leaves its responsibility scope diffuse or its result contract unnamed/unstable, satisfying child AC6 while failing parent AC3.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child AC6 (or add a companion AC) so that if the forcing case introduces a new subverb, the ticket also proves the subverb has a single coherent responsibility and a documented, stably named result contract validated by a schema/characterization test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance step to sweep and update/remove any docs, help text, or tooling that still reference reconcile-check or bridge_state/reconcile-check.json after migration.
evidence: AC-4: 'Persisted report behavior is migrated from bridge_state/reconcile-check.json ...'
Scope lists 'docs' but no AC requires removing/updating references to the retired reconcile-check command or report path.
findings.finding: Retiring/migrating the persisted report at bridge_state/reconcile-check.json and the reconcile-check command spelling may strand stale references (docs, help text, other tooling) that point to reconcile-check; the plan requires migration parity but not an explicit sweep for stranded references to the retired path/command.
findings.location: AC-4 and Scope ('persisted bridge-state reports, docs')
scenarios: Docs or tooling still reference bridge_state/reconcile-check.json after the report path moves.
Help text or runbooks continue to mention reconcile-check after its observables are routed to bridge subcommands.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define what constitutes an 'approved retirement' (approver + where recorded) or reword to a self-attestable 'documented retirement rationale' so it is evaluable in-session.
evidence: 'or an explicit approved retirement' — approver and record location unspecified.
findings.finding: AC1 permits 'an explicit approved retirement' for an observable but does not state who approves or where the approval is recorded, making the criterion's completion gate ambiguous and potentially dependent on an out-of-session approver.
findings.location: AC line 1: 'Every reconcile-check observable has a documented canonical bridge owner or an explicit approved retirement.'
scenarios: Executor cannot tell whether their own note constitutes 'approved' retirement or whether a maintainer sign-off is required.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'approved' with a concrete artifact, e.g. 'a retirement rationale recorded in the plan/PR description for each retired observable.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing (e.g. keep reconcile-check.json emitting during a deprecation window) for consumers of the reconcile-check command and bridge_state/reconcile-check.json.
evidence: 'Migrate report persistence away from bridge_state/reconcile-check.json while proving parity or recording explicit retirement for every field.'
No mention of rollback, deprecation window, or expand-contract sequencing for existing consumers of the persisted report or the reconcile-check command.
findings.finding: The plan performs a migration that retires the reconcile-check command's report path (bridge_state/reconcile-check.json) and its direct-engine output, but specifies no rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing for consumers currently reading that report or invoking the command.
scenarios: An external tool or script reads bridge_state/reconcile-check.json and breaks silently after migration.
Parity claim proves wrong post-merge and there is no defined way to revert.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether the old command/report is retained during a deprecation window (expand-contract) or removed outright, and give the revert path if parity fails.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that verifies the legacy reconcile-check command/direct-engine output is removed or deprecated (not just that observables are re-homed).
evidence: Scope: 'reconcile-check report construction and direct-engine output'
ACs verify owners, parity, and tests but none asserts the reconcile-check command/direct-engine output is retired or forwarded.
findings.finding: Scope names 'reconcile-check report construction and direct-engine output' as in-scope, but no acceptance criterion verifies that the old reconcile-check command/output is actually removed or deprecated — only that observables gain new owners. Migration removal side is unverified.
scenarios: Both the legacy reconcile-check output and the new bridge routing coexist indefinitely, defeating the migration intent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default for the new-subverb decision (e.g. 'prefer routing to preview/fsck/status; introduce a new subverb only if an observable maps to none, and enumerate any such observables up front').
evidence: 'Implement a new well-named bridge diagnostic subverb only if an observable does not coherently fit those owners.'
findings.finding: The approach defers a real design decision to the executor: 'Implement a new well-named bridge diagnostic subverb only if an observable does not coherently fit those owners.' Whether a new subverb is needed depends on investigation the plan does not resolve.
scenarios: Executor must decide mid-implementation whether preview/fsck/status suffice or a new subverb is warranted, with no pre-agreed tie-breaker beyond 'coherently fit'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the doc/ADR artifact (e.g. an ADR or bridge command reference) that records the observable-to-owner mapping and the rationale for any new bridge diagnostic subverb.
evidence: 'Implement a new well-named bridge diagnostic subverb only if an observable does not coherently fit those owners.'
AC-3: 'Any new bridge diagnostic subverb has one coherent responsibility and a stable named result contract.'
AC-1 requires a 'documented canonical bridge owner' but does not name the doc/ADR artifact.
findings.finding: The plan may introduce a new bridge diagnostic subverb (AC-3) but does not require capturing the architectural decision — which observable is owned by preview vs fsck vs status, and why a new subverb was or wasn't needed — in an ADR or design doc.
scenarios: A future maintainer cannot tell why a given diagnostic lives under status vs fsck without re-deriving the ownership rationale.
A new subverb's responsibility boundary is undocumented, inviting scope creep.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the online/offline boundary before assigning owners: state that fsck is offline (no Jira client) and specify, for each Jira-snapshot-derived observable (orphaned_jira, unbound_jira, orphaned_bindings, field-diff discrepancies), whether it goes to an online owner (preview) or to a new online diagnostic verb — do not route live-snapshot observables into offline fsck.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py:3 — 'Audits bridge state without a Jira client'; outputs are unknown_event_types / binding_drift / store_integrity
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_check.py:352-379 — orphaned_jira / unbound_jira / discrepancies are derived from `jira_snapshot`
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:237 — jira_snapshot = fetcher.compute_snapshot(...) requires a live Jira fetch (acli + credentials)
Plan Approach: 'field-diff information belongs with preview, integrity/bindings with fsck, and operational witnesses with status'
findings.finding: The Approach assigns binding/integrity observables to `bridge fsck`, but fsck is an offline audit ('Audits bridge state without a Jira client') while the reconcile-check binding/integrity observables (orphaned_bindings, orphaned_jira, unbound_jira, and the field-diff discrepancies) are computed from a LIVE Jira snapshot; fsck's owner surface cannot produce them, so the assignment cannot achieve field parity as written.
findings.location: Approach ('integrity/bindings with fsck') and AC line 'fsck exposes binding/integrity diagnostics'
scenarios: Executor routes orphaned_jira/unbound_jira to fsck and finds fsck has no Jira client to compute them, forcing either a scope-widening (fsck becomes online, breaking its contract) or a silent field drop
findings.suggested_fix: Split the assignment by data source: fsck owns only offline binding-index/store-integrity observables (matching its existing binding_drift/store_integrity outputs); route Jira-snapshot-derived counts (orphaned_jira, unbound_jira, discrepancies) to preview or to a single new online bridge-diagnostic verb, and record the split in the observable-to-owner matrix.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive, capability-grounded rationale for each owner assignment (what data each owner already has and why it can source the assigned observable) rather than a spelling/semantic-only justification.
evidence: Approach gives only spelling-based motivation ('cannot be guessed from command spelling') plus bare owner labels, with no rationale tying each observable to the owner's existing data inputs/contract
ABSENCE: no statement of why preview/fsck/status can each actually produce the observables assigned to them
findings.finding: The plan asserts a semantic 'belongs-with' rationale for each owner but states no data-flow/positive rationale validating the assignments against each owner's actual capability (online vs offline, existing result contract), which is why the fsck online/offline collision is not surfaced.
scenarios: Executor accepts the owner labels at face value and discovers mid-implementation that an owner cannot source its assigned observable

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reference ADR 0092 in the plan and reconcile the migration/retirement direction with its constraint that reconcile-check retains its route and that removing compatibility 'requires a separate deprecation decision ... this decision does not authorize removal'.
evidence: ADR 0092 (docs/adr/0092-bridge-primary-vocabulary-compatibility-adapters.md) states: 'Reconcile-check remains a real Mode member and retains its dedicated lock-free route' and 'Canonical bridge preview ... is not a spelling alias for reconcile-check'.
ADR 0092 Consequences: 'Removing compatibility requires a separate deprecation decision after real consumers have migrated; this decision does not authorize removal.'

The plan's AC4 ('Persisted report behavior is migrated ... or explicit retirement evidence') and Approach ('Migrate report persistence away ... or recording explicit retirement') contemplate migration/retirement but never cite ADR 0092 or acknowledge that removal is gated on a separate deprecation decision.
This is prior art internal to the repo that directly governs the plan's central move; leaving it unaddressed risks the plan authorizing a retirement that ADR 0092 says it cannot.
findings.finding: The plan migrates/retires the reconcile-check surface without considering ADR 0092, the accepted decision record that governs exactly this surface and constrains its retirement.
scenarios: Executor treats AC4's 'explicit approved retirement' as sufficient to drop the reconcile-check route/report, contradicting ADR 0092's separate-deprecation-decision gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Context/Approach note citing ADR 0092, and scope AC4 to report/format migration only (with parity), explicitly deferring any route/mode removal to a separate deprecation decision as the ADR requires.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reference ADR 0060 and specify the compatibility/rollback contract for migrating bridge_state/reconcile-check.json (old/new writer overlap, rollback behavior), as ADR 0060 requires for committed bridge-state format changes.
evidence: ADR 0060 (docs/adr/0060-bridge-state-format-changes.md): 'These are shared-store changes ... a bad rollback can resurrect a removed representation or lose the state ... They need one explicit compatibility and rollback contract.'
reconcile-check.json is written under repo_root/'bridge_state' (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:271), i.e. the committed bridge-state domain ADR 0060 governs.
The plan's Scope names 'persisted bridge-state reports' and AC4 requires parity or retirement evidence, but neither cites ADR 0060 nor its compatibility/rollback-contract requirement.
findings.finding: The plan migrates the persisted bridge_state/reconcile-check.json report without considering ADR 0060, which requires an explicit compatibility/rollback contract for changes to committed bridge_state formats.
scenarios: Report file relocated or removed on ephemeral runners with committed bridge_state, with no rollback contract, resurrecting or losing state on a bad rollback.
